title: Early Termination Fee Terms for Small Business Electricity Supply Agreements
content:
## Terms in force

1. A business early termination fee under Small Business Electricity Supply is assessed only once the agreement is drop pending or closed, as shown by the agreement record's status.
2. Only one early termination fee may be billed per business agreement; an early termination fee line already on the agreement's bill means the fee has been billed.
3. The remaining months are twelve times the difference in years plus the difference in months between the termination date and the contract end date, plus one when the day of the month of the contract end date is later than the day of the month of the termination date.
4. No fee applies when the termination date falls within the plan's free window of calendar days before the contract end date, equality counting as inside, or within the plan's automatic-renewal free days after the plan change date of an automatically renewed term, or within the plan's rescission window days after the utility confirmation date.
5. No fee applies when the plan waives the fee on an upgrade to a commercial and industrial contract and the drop reason is an upgrade to a commercial and industrial contract with a Beacon Ridge commercial and industrial contract on the same site in pending or active status.
6. Business closure, relocation, sale of the business and bankruptcy do not waive the fee; there is no state cap on business fees.
7. The fee method, damages rate, minimum fee, flat fee and free window are set per plan; each agreement reads the figures of its own plan.

## Retired clauses

The following clauses are **no longer in force**; each has been superseded and is not applied:

- "The termination date is the drop requested date for a cancellation and the close date for a switch-away or final bill."
- "Under the per-remaining-kWh method, the remaining kWh are the site's annual kWh usage times the remaining months divided by 12, rounded half up to a whole kWh, and the fee is the remaining kWh times the damages rate rounded half up to the cent, but not less than the minimum fee; under the flat method the fee is the flat fee; under the none method no fee applies."

## Remaining months, worked (hypothetical dates)

| Termination date | Contract end date | Years and months apart | Day-of-month step | Remaining months |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 March 2026 | 31 December 2026 | 0 years, 9 months | 31 is later than 10, so one is added | 10 |
| 20 March 2026 | 15 December 2026 | 0 years, 9 months | 15 is not later than 20 | 9 |
| 5 June 2025 | 5 June 2027 | 2 years, 0 months, so 24 | 5 is not later than 5 | 24 |

## Free window, at its boundary (hypothetical, 30-day free window, contract end 31 December)

| Termination date | Days before contract end | Fee |
|---|---|---|
| 1 December | 30 | none (equality counts as inside) |
| 30 November | 31 | the free window does not apply |

## Grounds that do not waive the fee

Closing the business, relocating, selling the business and bankruptcy are not grounds for waiver; no state cap limits a business fee.

superseded_clauses: The termination date is drop_requested_date for a cancellation and close_date for a switch-away or final bill.

Under the per_remaining_kwh method, etf_remaining_kwh is the site's annual_kwh_usage times etf_months_remaining divided by remaining_usage_divisor_months, rounded half up to a whole kWh, and the fee is etf_remaining_kwh times etf_rate_usd_per_kwh rounded per charge_rounding, but not less than etf_minimum_usd; under the flat method the fee is etf_flat_usd; under the none method no fee applies.
